textual.observation: A service presented as Microsoft Office setup support tells viewers that calling it will connect them to an expert who initiates a remote session with their PC to fix system issues.

evidence.quote: When you call us, you get connected to one of our experts who would initiate a remote session with your PC and fix your system issues with your approval
We are best support provider in UK for Microsoft Office Online, www.office.com/setup, office.com/setup 365, Microsoft Office Setup 2016, Office 365 Login, www.office.com/verify etc.

textual.context: Promotional service description. The remote session is stated to occur with the user's approval (ASR_0001). No explicit Microsoft affiliation is stated in these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The requested call is linked to remote access to a personal computer, while the service presents itself as Microsoft Office support; this relationship may require later assessment of the service's identity and remote-access context.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether the service is affiliated with Microsoft, what permissions are requested during the remote session, whether payment or sensitive information is collected, or what occurred after contact.

visual.observation: A webpage branded as “Office Setup” displays the headline “INSTALL AND UPGRADE MS OFFICE BY EXPERTS” and prominently shows toll-free phone numbers including “USA/CANADA - 1-800-610-3441” and “UK [PHONE]-3880,” with a yellow call button for the UK toll-free number.
visual.context: The frame shows a service-style webpage using Office-related wording and a call-to-contact presentation; whether it is official, third-party, promotional, or demonstrative is unclear from the sampled frame.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible Office-related support/upgrade claim is linked to a requested contact action by phone number, which conditionally merits review as an identity/support-related cue.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish who operates the webpage, whether the phone numbers were called, whether any support was provided, or whether the service is authorized by Microsoft.

visual.observation: A similar “Office Setup” webpage frame states “WELCOME TO OFFICE SETUP FOR YOUR COMPUTER” and again displays toll-free contact numbers for USA/Canada and UK, plus a prominent yellow UK toll-free call button.
visual.context: The page presents itself as Office setup support for a computer, with contact navigation and phone numbers; promotional versus informational context is unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The claimed Office setup support identity is paired with a request-like phone contact path, creating a review-relevant relationship between support branding and user action.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show any completed contact, payment, credential entry, authorization request, or verification of the page’s affiliation.

visual.observation: A services page lists Office setup-related items such as “www.office.com/setup,” “Office.com/setup sign in,” “Office Setup not working,” “Download Office,” “Microsoft Office Installation,” “Office 2010 Download,” “Office 2016 Download,” “Office.com/setup login,” and “Office Reinstall.”
visual.context: The page appears to aggregate Office setup, installation, login, download, product key, and reinstall support topics; whether these are links or service claims is visually suggested but not fully verifiable from the frame.
visual.potential_relevance: Office/Microsoft-branded setup and login/product-key topics are visibly associated with a support-services page, which conditionally merits review because support identity and potentially sensitive setup/account actions are presented together.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not show any user clicking these items, entering credentials or product keys, downloading software, or reaching a destination page.

visual.observation: A support-services section lists offerings including “Instant diagnose & repair,” “Data security and Integrity,” “Installing Operating System & other software,” “Performance optimization,” and “Updating your existing anti-virus to the latest version,” under an Office Setup-style site header with toll-free numbers.
visual.context: The frames show broad computer support and antivirus/OS support services presented under the same site header; no interaction is shown.
visual.potential_relevance: The Office Setup support presentation expands into broad PC repair/security services, implying a user support relationship that may involve installation, repair, or antivirus updating actions on a computer.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show remote access, software installation actually occurring, payment, permissions, or any claim about malware or data loss.

visual.observation: A pricing-plan section shows paid support plans in GBP with “BUY NOW” buttons, including visible prices such as “£199.99 GBP” and “£299.99 GBP,” durations of 90 days, support for multiple PCs, free software installation, PC clean-up tool, data recovery tool, and anti-malware.
visual.context: The frame presents commercial plan cards for computer support services; this is a visible purchase offer, not proof of payment or outcome.
visual.potential_relevance: Paid support plan pricing is linked to a “BUY NOW” action and bundled support/security/data-recovery benefits, making the money-flow relationship observable and conditionally review-relevant in the context of Office-related support pages.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show checkout details, payment recipient, terms beyond the visible plan bullets, whether the plans were purchased, or whether the advertised tools/services were delivered.

visual_context_notes.observation: Early frames show Microsoft Office application logos and names such as Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OneNote, Outlook, Publisher, and “Welcome to Office.”
Later frames show a physical Office-branded package or card with a key icon, but no readable product key or activation code is visible.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes an Office-support service through officesetups.co.uk, directs viewers to call displayed toll-free numbers, and says an expert will initiate a remote session with the caller's PC. It also presents paid plans with “BUY NOW” buttons, linking the support presentation to contact, remote access, and payment.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 is the closest available assigned subtype because the content presents paid service plans as an expansion path for the promoted support offering. The evidence supports paid plan access, but does not show commissions, downlines, team structures, matrices, uplines, or tier qualification.
